description: Shared anatomy facts for Tibi's 2D and 3D educational layers. deep_not_drawn retains the legacy 2D grouping; the 3D internal layers can include those muscles. Sources are factual references only: no source artwork or model is copied. The character is stylised, not an atlas; never use its geometry to teach exact attachment sites. Rig dimensions are original authoring choices, not measured human dimensions.

rendering_references.title: Muscles of the Pectoral Girdle and Upper Limbs
rendering_references.use: Broad lat/pectoral forms, upper-limb muscle regions and layers; factual guidance, not copied diagrams.

rendering_references.title: Anatomy, Shoulder and Upper Limb, Deltoid Muscle
rendering_references.use: Triangular three-part shoulder cap and convergence toward the deltoid tuberosity.

rendering_references.title: Brachialis Muscle, Elsevier Complete Anatomy
rendering_references.use: Distal anterior humerus belly, deep to biceps; no proprietary mesh or artwork reused.

rendering_references.title: Axial Muscles of the Abdominal Wall, and Thorax
rendering_references.use: Continuous paired rectus bands with intersections and broad abdominal wall layers.

rendering_references.title: Appendicular Muscles of the Pelvic Girdle and Lower Limbs
rendering_references.use: Thigh compartments, superficial gastrocnemius, broad deep soleus and anterolateral tibialis anterior.

muscles.name: Deltoid
muscles.note: 3D uses rounded-end triangular fans tapering into the upper arm, supported by a sloping shoulder envelope rather than an exposed joint orb. Inspect the actual posed contour, not only muscle volumes. Qualitative reference: statpearls-deltoid; dimensions remain illustrative.
muscles.origin: Lateral third of the clavicle, acromion and spine of the scapula
muscles.insertion: Deltoid tuberosity of the humerus
actions: Shoulder flexion and medial rotation (anterior fibres)
Shoulder extension and lateral rotation (posterior fibres)

muscles.name: Pectoralis major
muscles.note: 3D uses a broad fan across the chest, not a separate oval disc. Its lateral end converges toward the humerus with a rounded end wrapped onto the rib cage, and the clavicular edge sits lower than the defined lower border (1.12). Qualitative reference: openstax-upper.
muscles.origin: Medial clavicle, sternum and costal cartilages of ribs 1-6
muscles.insertion: Lateral lip of the intertubercular sulcus of the humerus

muscles.name: Biceps brachii
muscles.origin: Short head: coracoid process; long head: supraglenoid tubercle of the scapula
muscles.insertion: Radial tuberosity and bicipital aponeurosis

muscles.name: Triceps brachii
muscles.origin: Long head: infraglenoid tubercle of the scapula; lateral and medial heads: posterior humerus
muscles.insertion: Olecranon process of the ulna

muscles.name: Forearm flexor group
muscles.origin: Medial epicondyle of the humerus (common flexor origin)
muscles.insertion: Carpals, metacarpals and phalanges
muscles.note: A group, drawn as one shape.

muscles.name: Forearm extensor group
muscles.origin: Lateral epicondyle of the humerus (common extensor origin)
muscles.insertion: Metacarpals and phalanges
muscles.note: A group, drawn as one shape.

muscles.name: Rectus abdominis
muscles.note: 3D uses paired continuous bands with shallow intersections rather than six separate objects. Qualitative reference: openstax-trunk.
muscles.origin: Pubic crest and pubic symphysis
muscles.insertion: Xiphoid process and costal cartilages of ribs 5-7

muscles.name: External oblique
muscles.note: 3D relief stays embedded in the abdominal wall and follows the selected torso profile. Qualitative reference: openstax-trunk.
muscles.origin: External surfaces of ribs 5-12
muscles.insertion: Linea alba, pubic tubercle and anterior iliac crest
actions: Trunk rotation to the opposite side

muscles.name: Latissimus dorsi
muscles.note: 3D depicts a broad thin posterior fan, not a hanging flank spindle. No unvalidated elevation-only bulge is added. Qualitative reference: openstax-upper; exact attachment sites must not be inferred from the character.
muscles.origin: Spinous processes of T7-L5 via the thoracolumbar fascia, iliac crest and lower ribs
muscles.insertion: Floor of the intertubercular sulcus of the humerus

muscles.name: Trapezius
muscles.note: 3D uses embedded upper and lower portions instead of isolated neck knobs. Qualitative reference: openstax-upper.
muscles.origin: Occipital bone, ligamentum nuchae and spinous processes of C7-T12
muscles.insertion: Lateral clavicle, acromion and spine of the scapula

muscles.name: Erector spinae
muscles.origin: Sacrum, iliac crest and spinous processes of the lumbar and lower thoracic vertebrae
muscles.insertion: Ribs, transverse and spinous processes of the vertebrae, mastoid process
actions: Holds the spine upright against flexion under load
muscles.note: A group of three columns (iliocostalis, longissimus, spinalis), grouped schematically. 3D relief is embedded rather than an external rope; reference: openstax-trunk.

muscles.name: Gluteus maximus
muscles.origin: Posterior ilium, sacrum, coccyx and thoracolumbar fascia
muscles.insertion: Gluteal tuberosity of the femur and iliotibial tract

muscles.name: Quadriceps femoris
muscles.origin: Rectus femoris: anterior inferior iliac spine; vastus lateralis, medialis and intermedius: femur
muscles.insertion: Tibial tuberosity via the patella and patellar ligament
muscles.note: Four heads grouped in 2D; 3D uses named superficial/deep volumes within one thigh surface. Qualitative reference: openstax-lower.

muscles.name: Hamstrings
muscles.origin: Ischial tuberosity (biceps femoris short head: linea aspera of the femur)
muscles.insertion: Head of the fibula (biceps femoris); medial tibia (semitendinosus, semimembranosus)
muscles.note: Biceps femoris, semitendinosus and semimembranosus, grouped schematically. 3D volumes remain embedded in the posterior thigh envelope; reference: openstax-lower.

muscles.name: Hip adductor group
muscles.origin: Pubis and ischium
muscles.insertion: Linea aspera and adductor tubercle of the femur
actions: Adductor magnus also assists hip extension
muscles.note: Adductor magnus, longus and brevis, drawn as one shape.

muscles.name: Gastrocnemius
muscles.note: 3D tapers the two bellies toward the distal tendon while keeping them superficial to soleus. Qualitative reference: openstax-lower.
muscles.origin: Medial and lateral condyles of the femur
muscles.insertion: Calcaneus via the calcaneal (Achilles) tendon

muscles.name: Soleus
muscles.note: 3D depicts a broad, flatter deep volume rather than an outer calf lobe. Qualitative reference: openstax-lower.
muscles.origin: Head and upper shaft of the fibula, soleal line of the tibia
muscles.insertion: Calcaneus via the calcaneal (Achilles) tendon
actions: Ankle plantarflexion (works whatever the knee angle)

muscles.name: Tibialis anterior
muscles.note: 3D relief is anterolateral and integrated with the shin, not a central armour-like plate. Qualitative reference: openstax-lower.
muscles.origin: Lateral condyle and upper lateral shaft of the tibia
muscles.insertion: Medial cuneiform and base of the first metatarsal

muscles.name: Serratus anterior
muscles.note: 3D uses a thin sheet on the lateral rib wall that follows the flank, not a thick lateral slab; the old slab ended in a visible ledge under the arm (fixed 1.12). Digitations are not modelled. Qualitative reference: openstax-upper.
muscles.origin: Outer surfaces of the upper eight or nine ribs
muscles.insertion: Costal (front) surface of the medial border of the scapula
actions: Upward rotation of the scapula (with the trapezius)
Holds the scapula against the rib cage

muscles.name: Rhomboid major and minor
muscles.origin: Spinous processes of C7 to T5
muscles.insertion: Medial border of the scapula

muscles.name: Brachioradialis
muscles.origin: Lateral supracondylar ridge of the humerus
muscles.insertion: Styloid process of the radius
actions: Elbow flexion, strongest with the forearm mid-way between palm up and palm down

muscles.name: Infraspinatus (rotator cuff)
muscles.origin: Infraspinous fossa of the scapula
muscles.insertion: Greater tubercle of the humerus (middle facet)
actions: Stabilises the head of the humerus in the socket

muscles.name: Teres major
muscles.origin: Inferior angle of the scapula
muscles.insertion: Medial lip of the intertubercular groove of the humerus
actions: Shoulder adduction and medial rotation (with the latissimus dorsi)

deep_not_drawn.name: Iliopsoas
deep_not_drawn.origin: Lumbar vertebrae (psoas major) and iliac fossa (iliacus)

deep_not_drawn.name: Rotator cuff (supraspinatus, infraspinatus, teres minor, subscapularis)
deep_not_drawn.insertion: Greater and lesser tubercles of the humerus

deep_not_drawn.name: Brachialis
deep_not_drawn.insertion: Coronoid process and tuberosity of the ulna
deep_not_drawn.note: The 3D belly is on distal humerus, deep to biceps, not on the forearm. Reference: elsevier-brachialis. This list name is a legacy 2D convention.
actions: Elbow flexion in every forearm position

deep_not_drawn.name: Transversus abdominis
deep_not_drawn.origin: Iliac crest, thoracolumbar fascia, lower costal cartilages

deep_not_drawn.name: Gluteus medius
deep_not_drawn.note: 3D keeps it deep to gluteus maximus on the outer ilium, ending below the waistband; a wide lateral egg reaching the band read as a hip shelf (fixed 1.12). Qualitative reference: openstax-lower.
actions: Stabilises the pelvis in single-leg stance (running, walking, lunges)

deep_not_drawn.name: Brachialis
deep_not_drawn.origin: Distal half of the front of the humerus
deep_not_drawn.insertion: Coronoid process and tuberosity of the ulna
deep_not_drawn.note: The 3D belly is on distal humerus, deep to biceps, not on the forearm. Reference: elsevier-brachialis. This list name is a legacy 2D convention.
actions: Elbow flexion in every forearm position
